rationale: Facts: ismirsehregal reports that the header of Shiny's devmode JavaScript error dialog (added per NEWS.md for Shiny 1.8.1) is visually covered by {shinydashboard}'s fixed dashboardHeader, with a screenshot showing the occlusion and a second screenshot showing correct rendering in a plain basicPage app; both repros use devmode() plus a duplicated-input-id trigger. No comments. Classification hypothesis: bug -- a CSS stacking/positioning conflict between shiny's own error-dialog overlay and shinydashboard's fixed header, not a shinydashboard-authored defect. Duplicate check: no other open issue on this specific dialog/shinydashboard interaction found in this run's scanned batch. Wrong-location check: correct repo -- the error dialog markup and CSS are owned by shiny itself; shinydashboard is only the layout triggering the conflict, and shinydashboard is not on the triage allowlist. Regression check: no prior-version comparison is given (the dialog is a relatively new devmode feature), so not labeled regression. Reproduction plan: both provided code snippets are directly runnable and isolate the behavior via devmode() plus a duplicate-id warning. Impact: devmode-only cosmetic occlusion that can hide diagnostic error details for shinydashboard users during development; no production runtime impact. Priority: Low given it is dev-mode-only and a workaround (scrolling/resizing the dialog) is plausible. Recommended next action: label Priority: Low and mark ai-triage:done; a clear, reproducible CSS bug with no security or production implications, safe to label without further review.

title: Deep stack trace error (execution frame not found)
rationale: Facts: shikokuchuo reports that, once in roughly 50 runs of an app built on shinyrealtime/ggbot2 against current shiny main, an ordinary warning (rep_len: invalid 'length.out' value) escalated into an uncaught error while shiny was printing a stack trace, crashing the observer; full traceback and sessionInfo are included, but the reporter states the trigger is unknown and effectively random. Collaborator schloerke traced the warning to getCallNames()'s use of sapply/max(which(!hideable)) producing -Inf on an empty list, and flagged as an open question why the underlying `trace` value was NULL in the first place. Classification hypothesis: bug in conditions.R's stack-trace printing path that can convert a benign warning into a fatal, uncaught error when `trace` is unexpectedly NULL. Duplicate check: no other open issue on this printOneStackTrace/getCallNames interaction found in this run's scanned batch. Wrong-location check: correct repo -- the failing code (conditions.R) is shiny's own error-handling internals. Regression check: no older-release comparison is available; not labeled regression. Reproduction plan: the reporter cannot reliably reproduce it ("totally random", ~1/50 runs), and the maintainer's own root-cause comment ends on an open question about how `trace` becomes NULL, so a minimal, deterministic repro is still missing despite the productive diagnosis so far. Impact: when it occurs, an ordinary warning becomes an unhandled crash of the observer/app rather than a printed message, which is a meaningfully worse failure mode than the original warning, but the trigger condition is rare and not yet isolated. Priority: Medium given the crash-on-warning severity, offset by the very low observed frequency and lack of a confirmed trigger. Recommended next action: label Priority: Medium and needs reprex, and mark ai-triage:done; the maintainer is already engaged with concrete code pointers, so flagging the missing reliable reproduction is the correct low-risk signal rather than blocking on further AI action.

title: nav_menu in page_navbar has challenging keyboard navigation
rationale: Facts: emilydomanico, reviewing keyboard accessibility, reports that once keyboard focus enters a nav_menu dropdown inside page_navbar, there is no discoverable way to tab back out to the preceding/following top-level nav item -- Shift+Tab only closes the menu without reversing focus -- unlike plain Bootstrap 5.3 navbar dropdowns, which support normal tab traversal into and out of the menu. A minimal runnable repro and full R session info are included. No comments yet. Classification hypothesis: bug/accessibility defect -- a keyboard-trap-like focus-management gap in bslib's nav_menu component relative to upstream Bootstrap behavior. Duplicate check: no other open issue on nav_menu keyboard navigation found in this run's scanned batch. Wrong-location check: correct repo -- nav_menu/page_navbar markup and JS behavior are implemented in bslib, not in vanilla Bootstrap or shiny. Regression check: no prior-bslib-version comparison is given (the reporter compares against stock Bootstrap docs, not an older bslib release), so not labeled regression. Reproduction plan: the provided minimal app (page_navbar with a nav_menu of two panels) is directly runnable and isolates the focus behavior. Impact: real accessibility gap -- keyboard-only and screen-reader users can get stuck in the dropdown with no documented exit, which is a genuine usability barrier though not a functional/data-correctness bug. Priority: Medium given the accessibility significance of a potential keyboard trap, balanced against it not blocking core app functionality. Recommended next action: label Priority: Medium and mark ai-triage:done; a well-isolated, non-security, non-critical UI/accessibility bug safe to label without further review.

title: [Bug]: Busy indicator is not shown for `ui.output_ui`/`render.ui`
rationale: Facts: alinacherkas reports that with busy_indicators enabled, clicking an action button shows the busy spinner for an @render.data_frame output but not for a @render.ui output rendering a value_box, with a full runnable reprex and a shinylive link. A community commenter (authorAssociation NONE, not a maintainer) did a detailed byte-for-byte comparison of py-shiny's vendored shiny/www/shared/busy-indicators/busy-indicators.css against rstudio/shiny's shipped file and its scss source, concluding the spinner is deliberately suppressed on `.shiny-html-output:not(.shiny-table-output)` because such elements get `display:contents` (via bootstrap.min.css) and therefore have no box for the `::after` spinner to position against; the source scss comment explicitly says 'even if we could position it, we'd probably want to disable it if it has recalculating children.' Classification hypothesis: wrong location -- the suppression rule and its rationale live in a CSS file vendored byte-identically from rstudio/shiny (srcts/extras/busy-indicators/busy-indicators.scss), so a real fix likely needs to change shiny's upstream CSS/JS (e.g., a wrapper that generates a positionable box), not py-shiny-only code; py-shiny would only pick up the fix on its next vendored-assets sync. Duplicate check: no other open issue on missing busy spinners for output_ui found in this run's scanned batch. Wrong-location check: rstudio/shiny (this workflow's allowlisted repo) owns the vendored busy-indicators source; a py-shiny-only patch would fork the vendored file and be overwritten on the next sync. Regression check: no prior-version comparison is given; the suppression appears to be original, intentional (if surprising) design, not a regression. Reproduction plan: the reporter's shinylive app and inline reprex are directly runnable and clearly isolate the missing spinner on output_ui vs output_data_frame. Impact: moderate -- with spinner_type configured, users reasonably expect all recalculating outputs to show one; the commenter notes the P1 report is fair even though it is not a straightforward code defect. Priority: Medium given the real, if by-design, UX gap and its cross-package (shiny/py-shiny) scope. Recommended next action: label Priority: Medium and wrong location (target: rstudio/shiny, whose vendored CSS is the root cause), and mark ai-triage:needs-review; low confidence for automated sign-off since the wrong-location analysis comes from a non-maintainer and the actual fix design (a positionable wrapper) is still open.

title: Greeting message is mis-ordered when restoring a conversation from history
rationale: Facts: maintainer gadenbuie self-filed this, reporting that when a chat starts with an assistant greeting (via chat_ui(messages=), chat_append(), or chat_server(greeting=)) and the user has at least one real exchange, navigating away via the history navigator and back reorders the greeting to land after the user's first message instead of before it; includes a full runnable repro app plus confirmation via a scripted shinytest2 run driving the actual history-navigator UI, with the exact resulting (wrong) message order. The author also traces the likely root cause to extend_record_linear()'s fallback heuristic in chat_history_types.R, which sweeps turn-less UI messages (like the greeting, which never becomes an ellmer turn) onto the most-recently-created node instead of a dedicated leading node, with specific line references across chat_history_types.R, chat_history.R, and chat.R. Classification hypothesis: bug -- a concrete, self-diagnosed node-assignment defect in the history-restore path, not a persistence bug (the author notes the greeting is correctly saved). Duplicate check: no other open issue on greeting/message ordering during history restore found in this run's scanned batch. Wrong-location check: correct repo -- entirely within shinychat's R history-tree implementation. Regression check: no older-shinychat-release comparison is given (history/greeting restore appears to be existing functionality being newly scrutinized), so not labeled regression. Reproduction plan: the provided repro app plus the documented shinytest2-driven click sequence (load, send message, new conversation, switch back) is directly runnable and already confirmed by the author. Impact: moderate -- restored conversations display messages out of their original order, which is a real correctness/trust issue for a history feature even though no data is lost. Priority: Medium given the confirmed, well-diagnosed correctness defect in a user-facing history feature, without safety/security implications. Recommended next action: label Priority: Medium and mark ai-triage:done; maintainer-diagnosed with reproduction and precise code pointers, safe to label without further review.

title: Ship third-party license texts for the bundled JS assets
rationale: Facts: maintainer schloerke self-filed this, noting that pkg-py/src/shinychat/www/shinychat.js is a prebuilt 1.1MB bundle vendoring MIT-licensed react/react-dom/scheduler/use-sync-external-store (Meta) and use-stick-to-bottom (StackBlitz); esbuild's legal-comments block attributes these packages but points to a 'LICENSE file in the root directory of this source tree' that is not shipped -- only shinychat's own MIT LICENSE is included in the sdist, so MIT's requirement to accompany redistribution with the license text is not currently met. Cites conda-forge staged-recipes' explicit no-vendoring/license-inclusion checklist item as the trigger for noticing this, and proposes a concrete fix (emit a THIRDPARTY.txt at JS build time, ship it in sdist/wheel, verify via tar inspection, and follow up on the conda-forge feedstock's license_file entry). No comments. Classification hypothesis: bug/compliance -- a packaging-hygiene defect (incomplete license attribution for vendored dependencies) rather than a functional code bug. Duplicate check: no other open issue on bundled-JS license attribution found in this run's scanned batch. Wrong-location check: correct repo -- shinychat owns its own JS build and packaging. Regression check: not applicable, this is a packaging gap rather than a behavior change. Reproduction plan: the issue gives an exact reproduction (extract the sdist, grep the bundle's legal-comments block) confirming the missing license file. Impact: moderate -- a real open-source license-compliance gap, though the author notes it is being proceeded on as-is for the current conda-forge PR rather than treated as a hard blocker. Priority: Medium given the legal/compliance nature of an incomplete third-party license attribution, balanced against the author's own assessment that it isn't currently blocking. Recommended next action: label Priority: Medium and mark ai-triage:done; maintainer-authored with a concrete, low-risk proposed fix, safe to label without further review.
